_doc: WHAT WE ASK PLAID FOR, DECLARED HERE SO THE DASHBOARD IS VISIBLE TO CODE REVIEW.
On 21 Aug 2026 the item-products route was run against two real Items and both
reported consent to assets, identity, identity_match, liabilities, signal and
transactions. We request two of those. The other four came from the Plaid
dashboard's enabled-products configuration, which lives outside this
repository and which nothing here could see.
THAT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE. marginsheet_sync held 39 tables
against a description naming one job. marginsheet_app held plaid_items wider
than the column control that claimed to narrow it. Now our Items carry consent
wider than our request. ACTUAL REACH EXCEEDS STATED REACH BY DEFAULT, in every
system where something other than the code can grant it.
THE BILLING ARGUMENT IS IRRELEVANT (Guy, 21 Aug 2026). Consent is the
household permitting reach, and reach we do not use is reach we cannot justify
if asked. 'We could have read your identity but did not' is not a position to
SAME SHAPE AS edge-rules AND secret-inventory: declare what we intend, ask the
provider what is true, fail on the difference.

why.transactions: The ledger. Every figure in the product derives from it.
why.liabilities: Consented at link time and billed on first use, because a product cannot be added to an Item after creation without taking the household back through Link. The four Chase cards are exactly the case it exists for.

deliberatelyNotRequested.assets: Asset reports. Nothing calls /asset_report/*, and nothing in any spec plans to.
deliberatelyNotRequested.identity: Plaid identity. Our identity work is Better Auth plus Twilio Verify; the household's name and address come from them, not from the bank.
deliberatelyNotRequested.identity_match: Identity comparison. Same reasoning, and it would mean sending a household's details to a third party to be scored.
deliberatelyNotRequested.signal: ACH risk scoring. We move no money, so there is nothing to score.
deliberatelyNotRequested.investments: Would be required for ANY investment figure, since balances read 0.00 without it. It is a real decision rather than an omission and is tracked in docs/open-items.json.

grandfathered.reason: SoFi, relinked 21 Aug 2026 to obtain 730 days of history, before the dashboard narrowing. Not worth a second relink: nothing in this system calls assets, identity, identity_match or signal.
Chase, connected 21 Aug 2026, before the dashboard narrowing. Same reasoning.

grandfatheredWhy: ITEMS THAT CARRY WIDER CONSENT BY DECISION RATHER THAN BY DRIFT (Guy, 21 Aug 2026).
Plaid dashboard settings apply to an Item AT CREATION, so narrowing the
enabled products is FORWARD ONLY. These two Items were created before the
narrowing and keep consent to assets, identity, identity_match and signal.
The only way to change that is a relink, which costs a household trip through
Link to remove reach nothing uses.
THEY ARE LISTED SO THE CHECK TOLERATES THEM RATHER THAN FAILING. A check that
is red by design teaches people to ignore it, and an ignored check is worth
less than no check: it corrodes every true red beside it, which is the same
THE EXTRA PRODUCTS ARE STILL REPORTED. Tolerating is not hiding. The route
names them and says they are expected for this Item, so a reader sees the
state and the reason rather than a clean result that conceals both.
REMOVING AN ENTRY IS HOW THIS EXPIRES. If either Item is ever relinked, its
line comes out and the check goes back to full strictness for it.
